For an outage that could last overnight, I’d look at the **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)**. It has **2,073.6 Wh** of capacity; the cited estimate is about **a day for a 100 W ceramic heat emitter on a thermostat**. The exact runtime depends on how often the heater cycles and what else you plug in. ([Source and runtime estimates](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage))

For a smaller setup, the **BLUETTI Elite 30 V2** (288 Wh) is listed at roughly **6–8 hours with a 24 W heat mat**; for a 100 W emitter, the **BLUETTI AC180** (1,152 Wh) is estimated at **15–18 hours**. Those are better fits if your heater’s actual wattage and outage risk are lower.

Whichever you choose, run the heater through its **thermostat**, check the station’s rating against the heater’s wattage, and test your setup before an outage. Insulating the enclosure can help it hold heat longer. ([Petco’s outage guidance](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage))
